summary: Intermittent 403: 'sub' claim collision after Azure AD B2B token-exchange maps session to wrong tenant causing RBAC failures
description: Customer on a private deployment (HelioHealth) reports intermittent 403s for admin-console and API routes after enabling Azure AD B2B guest invitations. Issue appears after a user accepts B2B invite and signs in; sometimes their session is created but RBAC lookups return no role bindings, resulting in 403 Authorization failures. Customer sees this across multiple users and tenants, not correlated to a specific model or route.
impact: Several HelioHealth admins cannot access the Redwood Console or call admin APIs intermittently. Affects production users in us-east-1; customer reports degraded ops and blocked workflows for compliance-sensitive tasks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) HelioHealth invites external user via Azure AD B2B (guest); 2) User accepts invite and completes sign-in against HelioHealth tenant; 3) Fronting identity-proxy performs token-exchange to issue Redwood session token; 4) User attempts to access /console (admin) or call admin API; 5) Observe 403 returned intermittently with 'role binding not found' in logs.
logs: Identity-proxy request trace: request_id=ip-ctx-0d9f3a, incoming id_token claims: {"sub": "user:oid:1111", "email": "guest.user@example.com", "tid": "a1b2c3"}. After token-exchange we emit session cookie (session_id=sess-7f2b). RBAC lookup using cache key 'sub:user:1111' returned empty. Later a subsequent login for the same user produced id_token with sub 'guest.user@example.com' (email-as-sub) and RBAC lookup succeeded. See snippet: [identity-proxy.log: 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] "session-lookup key=sub:user:1111 -> MISS"; [rbac.log] "binds for tenant a1b2c3 not found for key sub:user:1111".
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced with HelioHealth testing account; observed two different 'sub' formats emitted by Azure AD in B2B flows depending on token audience and whether token came from token-exchange vs initial id_token.
- Our session-store keys sessions by raw 'sub' claim. RBAC resolution pipeline later normalizes principal to email and looks up role bindings by email; mismatch causes empty binding results.
- Cache layer (memcached) contains stale entry for some 'sub' variants leading to repeated failures until TTL expires.
- Hypothesis: Azure AD B2B sometimes returns pairwise subject (opaque oid) vs emails-as-sub depending on token version / conditional access or token-exchange parameters. Our code assumes 'sub' is stable across exchanges.
- Also saw one request path where identity-proxy performed a token-exchange with &client_id=legacy-client which returned different sub format.
mitigation_attempts: 1) Asked customer to reconfigure Azure AD token issuance to include stable 'email' claim as part of id_token and to prefer 'oid' consistently; 2) Temporary workaround: restart identity-proxy to clear memcached entries for HelioHealth tenant (restarted staging proxy and observed reduction in repro rate). 3) Added request-level fallback in session-lookup to attempt email-based RBAC lookup when 'sub' lookup misses (hotfix branch applied to canary).
comments: Priya Nair (Support): Collected sample tokens and requested logs from customer; escalated to ENG because this is an interoperability issue with Azure AD B2B.
Miguel Santos (SRE): Reproduced locally against customer's test tenant. Confirmed memcached entries for mixed sub formats. Working on a safe fallback in identity-proxy to attempt normalized lookups.
HelioHealth SRE (customer): We observed this for 4 of 12 invited guest users. Guest accounts sometimes work on retry. Happy to provide tenant logs and an invite pair for repro.
Jordan Blake (Eng): Rolling a canary hotfix that attempts email fallback and also logs both raw_sub and normalized_principal for future debugging.
Miguel Santos (SRE): Canary deployed hotfix to two gateways in us-east-1 at 2026-03-11T18:40Z. Initial telemetry shows 80% drop in 403s for affected users.
resolution_summary: Deployed identity-proxy hotfix (v1.9.3-canary -> v1.9.3) that: 1) normalizes principal resolution to prefer email claim if present, 2) falls back to alternate sub formats when RBAC lookup misses, and 3) emits detailed logging for sub/email/oid for future debugging. Cleared memcached keys for HelioHealth tenant and coordinated with customer to request consistent token format from Azure AD.
fix_deploy_notes: Hotfix rolled to canary 2026-03-11 18:40Z (2 gateways), verified reduced error rate. Full rollout to all us-east-1 gateways completed 2026-03-12 03:15Z. Added migration script to sweep session-store for mixed-format entries and normalize principal index.
followups: Engineering to add robust principal canonicalization in identity-proxy (ENG-5042).
Product to update Private deployment KB with Azure AD B2B recommendations (KB-Priv-AD-B2B).
Customer success to confirm HelioHealth reconfigures token issuance and reports back in 2 weeks.
